Infrastructure as Code with Pulumi on AWS

A public Nginx web container and an S3 static website, written in Python, deployed and then destroyed by Pulumi, with the state stored in a remote S3 backend.

◎Goal & architecture

Describe the infrastructure in a Python program, let Pulumi compute the plan and create the resources on AWS, check that they work, then delete everything.

Pulumi CLI v3.274.1Python 3.14pulumi-aws 7.54.0 AWS CLI 2.36.8Region eu-north-1ECS Fargate · ALB · S3

1AWS account setup

We create a dedicated IAM user (helmidev03) with an access key used only by the CLI, configured with aws configure. The keys stay in ~/.aws/credentials and never appear in the code.

IAM · create the user

  • New IAM user helmidev03, option Attach policies directly.
  • Policy AdministratorAccess is ticked, so the user can create any resource (ECS, Load Balancer, S3). Pulumi needs that.

IAM · create an access key

  • Use case Command Line Interface (CLI): the key is for programs (the aws command and Pulumi), not for the website.
  • The key (an ID + a secret) was saved on the PC with aws configure. It never appears in the code or in this report.

2Remote state backend

Pulumi records the list of resources it created in a state file. Instead of keeping it on the PC, we store it in a dedicated S3 bucket that the whole group can share:

  • private: Block Public Access enabled;
  • encrypted: SSE-S3 (AES-256);
  • versioned: every version of the state is kept, so we can roll back.

4The infrastructure code

Everything is described in __main__.py. Each Python object maps to one AWS resource:

ResourceRole
SecurityGroupFirewall: port 80 open to the Internet
LoadBalancer · TargetGroup · ListenerFixed public address that forwards HTTP :80 traffic to the container
ECS Cluster · TaskDefinition · ServiceRuns 1 nginx container on Fargate and keeps it running (0.25 vCPU, 512 MB)
S3 Bucket · BucketWebsiteConfigurationBucket in static website mode (index.html, error.html)
BucketPublicAccessBlock · BucketPolicyAllows public read only (s3:GetObject)
BucketObjectv2 ×3Uploads the files from the www/ folder

Outputs: nginx_url, site_url and site_bucket.

Show the full code (__main__.py)
tp3-iac/__main__.py
"""TP3 - IaC with Pulumi (AWS, Python)
1) An Nginx web container on ECS Fargate, exposed publicly through a Load Balancer (port 80)
2) An S3 bucket configured to host a static website
"""
import json
import mimetypes
import os

import pulumi
import pulumi_aws as aws

# ───────────────────────── Network (default VPC) ─────────────────────────
vpc = aws.ec2.get_vpc(default=True)
subnets = aws.ec2.get_subnets(filters=[{"name": "vpc-id", "values": [vpc.id]}])

# Firewall: open port 80 (HTTP) to the whole Internet
web_sg = aws.ec2.SecurityGroup(
    "web-sg",
    vpc_id=vpc.id,
    description="HTTP public (port 80)",
    ingress=[{"protocol": "tcp", "from_port": 80, "to_port": 80, "cidr_blocks": ["0.0.0.0/0"]}],
    egress=[{"protocol": "-1", "from_port": 0, "to_port": 0, "cidr_blocks": ["0.0.0.0/0"]}],
)

# ───────────────────────── 1. Nginx container ─────────────────────────
# Public Load Balancer = fixed address reachable from the Internet
alb = aws.lb.LoadBalancer(
    "nginx-alb",
    load_balancer_type="application",
    security_groups=[web_sg.id],
    subnets=subnets.ids,
)
target_group = aws.lb.TargetGroup(
    "nginx-tg",
    port=80,
    protocol="HTTP",
    target_type="ip",
    vpc_id=vpc.id,
    health_check={"path": "/"},
)
listener = aws.lb.Listener(
    "http-listener",
    load_balancer_arn=alb.arn,
    port=80,
    default_actions=[{"type": "forward", "target_group_arn": target_group.arn}],
)

# ECS cluster + task definition (official nginx image)
cluster = aws.ecs.Cluster("tp3-cluster")
task = aws.ecs.TaskDefinition(
    "nginx-task",
    family="nginx",
    cpu="256",
    memory="512",
    network_mode="awsvpc",
    requires_compatibilities=["FARGATE"],
    container_definitions=json.dumps([{
        "name": "nginx",
        "image": "public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx:latest",
        "essential": True,
        "portMappings": [{"containerPort": 80, "protocol": "tcp"}],
    }]),
)

# Service: keeps 1 container running and registers it behind the Load Balancer
service = aws.ecs.Service(
    "nginx-svc",
    cluster=cluster.arn,
    task_definition=task.arn,
    desired_count=1,
    launch_type="FARGATE",
    network_configuration={
        "subnets": subnets.ids,
        "security_groups": [web_sg.id],
        "assign_public_ip": True,
    },
    load_balancers=[{
        "target_group_arn": target_group.arn,
        "container_name": "nginx",
        "container_port": 80,
    }],
    opts=pulumi.ResourceOptions(depends_on=[listener]),
)

# ───────────────────────── 2. S3 bucket (static website) ─────────────────────────
site_bucket = aws.s3.Bucket("site-bucket", force_destroy=True)

# Allow a public (read-only) bucket policy on THIS bucket
public_access = aws.s3.BucketPublicAccessBlock(
    "site-public-access",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    block_public_acls=True,
    ignore_public_acls=True,
    block_public_policy=False,
    restrict_public_buckets=False,
)

# "Static website" mode
website = aws.s3.BucketWebsiteConfiguration(
    "site-website",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    index_document={"suffix": "index.html"},
    error_document={"key": "error.html"},
)

# Everyone can READ the files (s3:GetObject), nobody can write
aws.s3.BucketPolicy(
    "site-policy",
    bucket=site_bucket.id,
    policy=site_bucket.arn.apply(lambda arn: json.dumps({
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [{
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Principal": "*",
            "Action": "s3:GetObject",
            "Resource": f"{arn}/*",
        }],
    })),
    opts=pulumi.ResourceOptions(depends_on=[public_access]),
)

# Upload the files from the www/ folder into the bucket
for name in os.listdir("www"):
    aws.s3.BucketObjectv2(
        name,
        bucket=site_bucket.id,
        key=name,
        source=pulumi.FileAsset(os.path.join("www", name)),
        content_type=mimetypes.guess_type(name)[0] or "text/plain",
    )

# ───────────────────────── Outputs ─────────────────────────
pulumi.export("nginx_url", pulumi.Output.concat("http://", alb.dns_name))
pulumi.export("site_bucket", site_bucket.bucket)
pulumi.export("site_url", pulumi.Output.concat("http://", website.website_endpoint))

In the browser

Nginx, through the Load Balancer

  • The address is the Load Balancer's public name (the nginx_url output): nginx-alb-…elb.amazonaws.com.
  • Welcome to nginx! is Nginx's default page: the container is running and reachable from the Internet.

Static website, from the S3 bucket

  • The address is the bucket's website endpoint (the site_url output): site-bucket-…s3-website.eu-north-1.amazonaws.com.
  • The page is our www/index.html, uploaded by Pulumi. There is no server: S3 itself hands out the file.

Error page

  • /error.html is the 404 page set in the bucket's website configuration.
  • S3 shows it automatically for any file that does not exist in the bucket.

In the AWS console: the Nginx side

A visitor goes through these pieces, in this order:

Browser→Load Balancer · listener :80→ Target group→Task = nginx container

The task runs inside the cluster. The service keeps it alive and writes its address into the target group, which is what links the Load Balancer to the container.

ECS · the cluster

  • One cluster, tp3-cluster-f219f31. Pulumi added the random ending -f219f31 to the name.
  • 1 service and 1 task running.
  • 0 EC2: there is no server to manage, because Fargate provides the machine.

ECS · the service inside the cluster

  • Service nginx-svc-fd7080c: Active, launch type Fargate.
  • 1/1 tasks running: we asked for 1 container and 1 is running. If it crashed, the service would start a new one.
  • Task definition nginx:1 is the container's recipe card (version 1).

ECS · the service's task

  • Task 2dbed7fc… is the running container, started by the service.
  • Last status Running.
  • “Health status: Unknown” only means no check was set inside the container. The Load Balancer's check (below) is the one that matters.

ECS · the task's details

  • Image public.ecr.aws/nginx/nginx:latest: the official Nginx, downloaded from AWS's public registry.
  • Size: 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB, launch type Fargate.
  • Lifecycle: created → image downloaded (5 s) → Running at 10:23.

EC2 · the Load Balancer

  • nginx-alb-d664ab3 is Active and Internet-facing. Its DNS name is the address we opened in the browser.
  • It is spread over the 3 subnets of the default VPC (eu-north-1a, 1b, 1c).
  • Listener HTTP:80 → forwards 100% of visitors to target group nginx-tg-f0c898f.

ECS · the Load Balancer sees the container

  • Target nginx:80 in target group nginx-tg-f0c898f: 1 healthy, 0 unhealthy.
  • The Load Balancer regularly opens page / on the container, and the container answers.
  • This proves the Load Balancer really sends visitors to our container.

In the AWS console: the S3 side

S3 · the two buckets

  • site-bucket-94f71b4: the static website bucket, created by Pulumi at 10:20.
  • tp3-pulumi-state-401046276523: the state bucket, created earlier (10:15) with the aws command.
  • Both are in Stockholm (eu-north-1).

NAME  LAST UPDATE   RESOURCE COUNT
dev*  1 minute ago  16

S3 · the state file

  • .pulumi/stacks/tp3-iac/dev.json is Pulumi's state for stack dev: the list of everything it created.
  • 34.1 KB, last modified at 10:23:05, right when pulumi up finished.
  • Bucket versioning Enabled: older versions of the state are kept.

Inside dev.json: what Pulumi remembers

  • We downloaded the version saved at 10:23:05 (34,914 bytes), right after pulumi up. Versioning keeps every older version, which is useful here because the current one (after destroy) is almost empty.
  • stack: organization/tp3-iac/dev. This file belongs to project tp3-iac, stack dev.
  • secrets_providers: passphrase. Only a salt is stored, never the passphrase itself.
  • outputs (highlighted in green): the 3 values printed at the end of pulumi up.
  • resources: 16 entries, which are the stack, the AWS provider (the plugin Pulumi uses to talk to AWS) and the 14 AWS resources. The last command lists them as type · name in the code · real ID on AWS, for example web-sg → sg-07b41981ec59b6c60. This is how pulumi destroy knows exactly what to delete.

★Key takeaways

IaCInfrastructure is code: reproducible, versioned in Git and reviewable by the team.
PulumiA real programming language (Python). preview shows the plan before acting, and up only applies the differences.
Remote stateThe S3 backend shares the state between group members and protects it (private, encrypted, versioned).
Cost controldestroy deletes everything that was created, so no forgotten resource keeps costing money.
